questions.question_text: By what date must a WV real estate license be renewed each year to avoid expiring?
questions.explanation: 174-1-8.1: "All licenses expire on June 30 regardless of the date the license was issued." The license term coincides with the fiscal year (§30-40-17(c)(5)). The WVREC opens its online renewal portal on May 1, but June 30 is the operative deadline; after that the license is expired and late fees apply through December 31.

questions.question_text: A licensee misses the June 30 renewal deadline. What additional fee must they pay if they renew by August 31?
questions.explanation: Late renewal fees are tiered and are charged in addition to the renewal fee: $50 from July 1 through August 31, $75 from September 1 through October 31, and $100 from November 1 through December 31 (174-2-2.5). A license not renewed on or before December 31 cannot be renewed at all. Practising on an expired license is separately sanctionable (174-1-8.2).

questions.question_text: WV license renewals are processed through which system?
questions.explanation: License renewals are completed through the WVREC's Online License Renewal System. This is separate from the initial application system.

questions.question_text: How often must WV real estate licenses be renewed?
questions.explanation: WV requires annual license renewal between May 1 and June 30. This is more frequent than many states that use biennial (every 2 years) renewal cycles.

questions.question_text: A salesperson fails to renew by December 31. What happens to their license?
questions.explanation: 174-1-8.3: the license of a licensee who does not renew on or before December 31 of the year the license expired "shall be cancelled and the licensee shall be required to comply with all the requirements for obtaining a new license, including the examination requirement." §30-40-4 defines "cancelled" the same way.

questions.question_text: A WV licensee is no longer associated with a broker. What is their license status?
questions.explanation: §30-40-4 defines "inactive" as a licensee who is not authorized to conduct any real estate business and is not required to comply with any continuing education requirements. Inactive certificates are held by the Commission (174-1-9.2), and returning to active status requires furnishing the CE that would have been required (174-1-8.5.b).

questions.question_text: Which license status allows a WV licensee to actively practice real estate?
questions.explanation: Only an active license allows practice. Active status requires both a current license and association with an employing broker.

questions.question_text: In West Virginia, what is the difference between an 'expired' license and a 'cancelled' license?
questions.correct_answer: Expired means not renewed by July 1; cancelled means still not renewed by December 31
distractors: Cancelled means not renewed by July 1; expired means still not renewed by December 31
Both terms mean the same license status
Cancelled is voluntary; expired is involuntary
questions.explanation: Both are defined in §30-40-4. "Expired" means a license that was not renewed by July 1 — the day after the June 30 deadline. "Cancelled" means a license that was not renewed by December 31 of the year in which the license expired. So expiration comes first and can still be cured with a late fee; cancellation is the further lapse and requires reapplying and re-examining.

questions.question_text: A salesperson on inactive status receives a request to show property. Can they legally do so?
distractors: Yes, with the listing broker's permission
Yes, as long as they don't negotiate
questions.explanation: An inactive license means the licensee cannot practice real estate in any capacity, including showing property. They must associate with a broker and activate their license first.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized WV license status?
questions.explanation: WV recognizes four license statuses: active, inactive, canceled, and expired. 'Provisional' is not a valid WV license status.

questions.question_text: How many hours of continuing education must WV licensees complete per fiscal year?
questions.explanation: §30-40-16(a) requires every licensee to complete seven hours of continuing professional education for each fiscal year, "with each hour equaling 50 minutes of instruction." The minimum length of an approved CE course is three hours (174-3-3.5.3).

questions.question_text: A licensee takes a CE course on contract law this year. Can they repeat the same course next year for CE credit?
questions.correct_answer: No, not the same course as the previous renewal
distractors: Yes, any approved course counts each year
No, an approved course may never be taken twice
questions.explanation: 174-1-8.6: "The courses taken to satisfy the then-current continuing education requirement shall not be the same as courses taken for the previous license renewal." The comparison is to the immediately preceding renewal, so the same course cannot be used two years running. The Commission may audit any licensee's CE (174-1-8.7).

questions.question_text: A new licensee passed both exam sections in May and their first renewal is due June 30 of the same fiscal year. Must they complete CE?
questions.explanation: Licensees who passed both exam sections during the fiscal year of their first required renewal are exempt from CE for that initial period if they renew by June 30.

questions.question_text: Who must provide continuing education courses for WV licensees?
distractors: The WVREC directly, no outside providers
Any licensed broker with 10+ years experience
questions.explanation: CE courses must be offered by Commission-approved providers and taught by Commission-approved instructors, with approval obtained before the course is advertised or offered (§30-40-16(d)). One shortcut: real estate-related CE provided or approved by the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing and Certification Board, the Division of Highways, the West Virginia State Bar, or another agency of the state is recognized as approved (§30-40-16(e)).

questions.question_text: Brokers and associate brokers must include how many broker-level CE hours within their 7-hour annual requirement?
questions.explanation: §30-40-16(a): "For brokers and associate brokers, three of the required seven hours shall be from the broker-level education curriculum approved by the commission." Salespersons have no mandatory-topic split — all seven of their hours may be electives.

questions.question_text: When a WV salesperson changes employing brokers, whose duty is it to apply to the WVREC for the change?
distractors: No application is required, only a courtesy notice
questions.explanation: §30-40-17(b)(2) puts the duty on the licensee: an associate broker or salesperson shall "promptly make application to the commission of any change of employing broker." 174-1-9.4 spells out the steps — the licensee first notifies the current responsible broker in writing, submits the prescribed change-of-responsible-broker application, and pays the $20 fee. The departing broker must immediately return the license certificate to the Commission (174-1-9.3), and the new broker supplies a sworn statement confirming the transfer (174-1-9.5).

questions.question_text: A salesperson leaves Broker A and joins Broker B. What must happen with WVREC?
questions.correct_answer: The transfer must be reported to WVREC
distractors: The salesperson must retake the exam
questions.explanation: The salesperson must apply to the Commission for the change of responsible broker, notify the current broker in writing, and pay the $20 change-of-employing-broker fee (§30-40-17(b)(2); 174-1-9.4; 174-2-2.6). The departing broker returns the license certificate to the Commission and the new broker files a sworn statement confirming the transfer.

questions.question_text: During the period between leaving one broker and joining another, what is the salesperson's license status?
questions.explanation: §30-40-17(b)(2) is explicit: "it shall be unlawful to perform any act contained in this article, either directly or indirectly, after affiliation has been terminated until the associate broker or salesperson has made application to the commission for a change of affiliated broker and the application is approved." Applying is not enough — the licensee must wait for approval.

questions.question_text: Can a WV salesperson be affiliated with more than one brokerage at the same time?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, with a separate license and certificate for each brokerage
distractors: No, only one employing broker at a time is permitted
Yes, but only with a written waiver from the WVREC
Yes, and one license certificate covers all affiliations
questions.explanation: 174-1-4.8, "Multiple concurrent licenses": "Licensees who choose to be affiliated with more than one brokerage must have a license and license certificate for each brokerage. These additional licenses have no additional requirements other than the payment of the appropriate license fee." Each affiliation is its own license, and the licensee still acts only under the responsible broker named on the certificate being used.

questions.question_text: A salesperson transfers from one brokerage to another. Must they complete additional education to effect the transfer?
questions.correct_answer: No, just report the transfer to WVREC
distractors: Yes, must retake the state exam portion
questions.explanation: No education or examination is required to transfer. What is required: written notice to the current responsible broker, the prescribed change-of-responsible-broker application, the $20 fee (174-2-2.6), and the new broker's sworn statement confirming the transfer. The licensee may not practise until the application is approved.
